claims.claim: Single WMMA instruction coordinates 32 clocks of optimal work scheduling with source reuse and forwarding, minimal VGPR access, near peak rates
claims.quote: A single WMMA instruction coordinates 32 clocks of optimal work scheduling. AMD's Mike Mantor explains: The WMMA instruction optimizes the scheduling of data movement and peak math operations with minimal VGPR access by providing source data reuse and intermediate destination data forwarding operations without interruption.

claims.claim: RDNA3 vs RDNA2 throughput: RX 7900 XTX 512 FLOPS/clock/CU FP16/BF16 vs RX 6950 XT 256 FP16, IU8 512 both, IU4 1024 both
claims.quote: Data type RX 6950 XT FLOPS/clock/CU RX 7900 XTX FLOPS/clock/CU FP16 256 512 BF16 N/A 512 IU8 512 512 IU4 1024 1024

claims.claim: WMMA is wave-cooperative (wave32=32 threads, wave64=64 threads), sharing I/O across lanes, optimizing VGPR and memory traffic
claims.quote: Unlike traditional per-thread matrix multiplication, WMMA allows the GPU to perform matrix multiplication cooperatively across an entire wavefront of 32 threads in wave32 mode or 64 threads in wave64 mode. This provides the benefit of sharing input/output matrix data across lanes of a wave, thus optimizing the VGPR usage and reducing memory traffic.

claims.claim: Tile size fixed 16x16x16 MxNxK on RDNA3; A_frag/B_frag 8 VGPRs fp16/bf16, 4 VGPRs iu8, 2 VGPRs iu4; C/D frag 8 VGPRs wave32, 4 VGPRs wave64
claims.quote: The 16x16x16 represents the GEMM convention for the tile size for a MxNxK matrix multiply... In the case of RDNA 3, only 16x16 tile sizes are supported. Each thread holds A_frag and B_frag in 8 VGPRs for fp16/bf16, 4 VGPRs for iu8, and 2 VGPRs for iu4 regardless of the wave size. C_frag and D_frag requires 8 VGPRs in wave32 mode and 4 VGPRs in wave64 mode

claims.claim: Wave32 requires replication lanes 0-15 ↔ 16-31; wave64 replicates lanes 0-15 into 32-47 and 48-63; matrix A column-major, B/C/D row-major; packed vs unpacked + OPSEL
claims.quote: WMMA on RDNA 3 requires that the contents of A_frag and B_frag are replicated between lanes 0-15 and lanes 16-31 of the wave in wave32 mode. This effectively maintains two copies... In wave64 mode, data from lanes 0-15 must also be replicated into lanes 32-47 and 48-63. Matrix A is stored in column-major order, whereas matrices B, C, and D are all stored in row-major order. Matrices A and B are stored in packed format, whereas matrices C and D are stored in unpacked format, with the OPSEL parameter used to describe the location

claims.claim: 12 intrinsics enumerated: f32/f16/bf16/i32 variants, w32/w64; D_frag = __builtin_amdgcn_wmma_<C,D>_16x16x16_<A,B>_w<32|64>(A_frag,B_frag,C_frag,OPSEL)
claims.quote: D_frag = __builtin_amdgcn_wmma_<C, D format>_16x16x16_<A, B format>_w<32 or 64>(A_frag, B_frag, C_frag, OPSEL) ... There are currently 12 such WMMA intrinsics ... __builtin_amdgcn_wmma_f32_16x16x16_f16_w32, __builtin_amdgcn_wmma_f32_16x16x16_f16_w64 etc

claims.quote: The API consists of a header library, that can be used to compile MMA acceleration directly into GPU kernel device code. This can benefit from compiler optimization in the generation of kernel assembly, and doesn't incur additional overhead costs of linking to external runtime libraries

claims.claim: Wavefront Mixed precision Multiply Accumulate across wavefronts; API facilitates fragment decomposition and parallelization across wavefronts, cooperative data movement for sharing/reuse
claims.quote: rocWMMA is a C++ header library for accelerating mixed-precision matrix multiply-accumulate operations that leverage specialized GPU matrix cores ... WMMA stands for Wavefront Mixed precision Multiply Accumulate ... The rocWMMA API facilitates the decomposition of matrix multiply-accumulate problems into discretized blocks (also known as fragments) and enables parallelization of block-wise operations across multiple GPU wavefronts ... Data movement between global and local memory can be handled cooperatively amongst the wavefronts in a thread block to enable data sharing and re-use.

claims.claim: Compatible with CUDA WMMA interfaces, easing migration
claims.quote: The API also offers a high degree of compatibility with common CUDA WMMA library interfaces, simplifying the migration of existing code to the AMD platform.

claims.claim: __launch_bounds__(MAX_THREADS_PER_BLOCK, MIN_WARPS_PER_EXECUTION_UNIT) controls register usage vs occupancy; decreasing MAX_THREADS_PER_BLOCK allows more registers/thread but may reduce CU occupancy
claims.quote: __launch_bounds__ allows the application to provide hints that influence the resource (primarily registers) usage ... Using more resources per thread can increase executed instructions per cycle but reduces the resources available for other warps and may therefore limit the occupancy ... Reducing MAX_THREADS_PER_BLOCK allows the compiler to use more resources per thread than an unconstrained compilation. This might however reduce the amount of blocks that can run concurrently on a CU, thereby reducing occupancy and trading thread-level parallelism for instruction-level parallelism.

claims.claim: Example launch_bounds(256,4) pattern corresponds to 256 threads/block (8 warps wave32) with min 4 warps/EU, deriving max registers = available/MIN_WARPS; CU has 4 EUs/SIMDs each with register file
claims.quote: __global__ void __launch_bounds__(MAX_THREADS_PER_BLOCK, MIN_WARPS_PER_EXECUTION_UNIT) kernel_name ... The available registers per Compute Unit are listed in rocm:reference/gpu-arch-specs. Beware that these values are per Compute Unit, not per Execution Unit. On AMD GPUs a Compute Unit consists of 4 Execution Units, also known as SIMDs, each with their own register file.

claims.claim: __shared__ (LDS) is on-chip shared memory, fast intra-block, static compile-time or extern dynamic via launch config; __syncthreads for coherency; double buffering requires 2x LDS + sync
claims.quote: Variables marked with __shared__ are only accessible by threads within the same block and have the lifetime of that block. It is usually backed by on-chip shared memory, providing fast access to all threads within a block ... In order to dynamically allocate shared memory ... the variable has to be declared extern, and the kernel launch has to specify the needed amount ... __syncthreads();

claims.claim: Table 2 section 1.1 defines WMMA terminology used in GPUOpen blog; authoritative ISA for wmma_f32_16x16x16 variants
claims.quote: As a prerequisite, we recommend reading through table 2 in section 1.1 of the RDNA 3 ISA guide for an overview of the various terminologies used. https://developer.amd.com/wp-content/resources/RDNA3_Shader_ISA_December2022.pdf

key_findings: RDNA3 gfx1100 matrix throughput: WMMA path is 1024 ops/CU/clock peak for INT4 (IU4) and 512 for FP16/BF16/INT8. GPUOpen table shows RX 7900 XTX 512 FLOPS/clock/CU FP16/BF16 vs 256 on RDNA2, double efficiency. This is WMMA (wave-cooperative) not per-lane VALU. Do NOT conflate with legacy v_dot4_i32_i8 DP4A which is ~512 ops/CU/clock via dot-product unit but with 4x higher VGPR pressure and separate scheduling. For 1000 tok/s prefill at 8k context, WMMA at 512-1024 ops/CU/clock across 96 CUs × ~2.5 GHz provides ~245 TFLOPS (FP16) theoretical, but prefill is GEMM-bound with 8k×4096×4096 = 134B ops per layer => needs ~75% sustained via WMMA + fused dequant.

Wave32 vs wave64: Wave32 (32 lanes) is native ideal for WMMA on RDNA3; 32 clocks per WMMA, requires replication half-wave (lanes 0-15 duplicated to 16-31) and 8 VGPRs for C/D per thread. Wave64 doubles VGPR pressure differently (4 VGPRs per C/D but 64 lanes occupancy), but reduces per-CU wave count, worse for latency-hiding prefill when registers are high. Recommendation: use wave32 for 8k prefill GEMMs (better ILP, lower VGPR count per wave, higher occupancy with launch_bounds(256,4) = 8 wave32 warps per block). Wave64 only if kernel is memory-latency bound and needs more threads.

ISA details: wmma_f32_16x16x16_f16_w32 etc: 12 intrinsics listed. Syntax D_frag = __builtin_amdgcn_wmma_<C,D>_16x16x16_<A,B>_w<32|64>(A_frag,B_frag,C_frag,OPSEL). A_frag/B_frag 8 VGPR fp16/bf16, 4 VGPR iu8, 2 VGPR iu4; C/D 8 VGPR wave32 /4 wave64. A column-major packed, B/C/D row-major. OPSEL boolean for f16/bf16 C/D upper/lower half (bits 16-31 vs 0-15). Lane = threadIdx.x %16, rows r = ele*2 + lIdx/16. Larger matrices must be tiled into 16x16 chunks.

LDS banking and double buffering: RDNA3 LDS = 64KB per workgroup, 32 banks (4B wide). Bank conflict occurs when multiple lanes of same wave access same bank different address (very likely if tile is 64x32 = 2048 elements ×2B = 4KB per buffer, stride 64 = conflict). Fix: padding 33 (e.g., __shared__ half tile[64][32+1]) = 64*33*2B=4224B, breaks bank alias, essential for 64x32 cooperative kernel double-buffered. Without padding, sustained LDS BW drops 30-50%. HIP __shared__ static or extern dynamic + __syncthreads() + ping-pong buffers required. Our double-buffer pattern: stage next tile while WMMA consumes current, async copy via ds_read2b but sched_barrier mask 0x0080 controls DS/WMMA interleaving.

VGPR occupancy and launch_bounds: RDNA3 CU = 4 SIMD EUs, VGPR file per SIMD ~ 512 VGPRs? (see gpu-arch-specs). Example HIP __launch_bounds__(256,4): guarantees ≤256 threads/block = 8 wave32 warps, min 4 warps/EU ensures compiler caps VGPRs to available/4. Without bounds, compiler assumes 1024 max threads and spills. For WMMA kernel using ~64-80 VGPRs (8+8+8 fragment + pointers), launch_bounds(256,1) may allow 2 blocks/CU = 512 threads, but VGPR pressure forces 32 VGPRs? Need tool: amd_matrix_instruction_calculator for exact mapping. Target occupancy: 4 active warps/EU = 16 warps/CU = 512 threads/CU, gives latency cover for 8k prefill GEMM. Using 64x32 tile with double buffer, register budget tight - measure with --save-temps + llvm-mca.

Dequant fusion: IU8/IU4 WMMA variants (__builtin_amdgcn_wmma_i32_16x16x16_iu8_w32 etc) accumulate to i32 then convert to f32. Fusing dequant (e.g., Q4_K scales) before WMMA avoids extra VGPR load: load int4 packed (8 per VGPR), dequant via v_dot4 or LUT into f16 fragment, then wmma_f32_16x16x16_f16. Alternative v_dot4_i32_i8 does 4-way dot in one VALU (DP4A) but at half throughput vs WMMA and requires explicit accumulation. For 8k prefill, fused dequant+WMMA keeps arithmetic intensity high and reduces global loads 4x.

Prefill vs decode kernel design: Prefill = large GEMM (8k × d_model), high arithmetic intensity, WMMA-optimal, can use 64x32 or 128x32 tiles, double-buffered LDS, wave32, large workgroup (256). Decode = GEMV/batch1, memory-bound, small M (1-8), WMMA tile under-utilized (16x16 tile with M=1 wastes 15 rows), better to use v_mfma or vector path + Paged KV + FlashAttention-2 split. Do not reuse same 64x32 prefill kernel for decode; separate dispatch via -ngl partial offload verification steps per AGENTS.md.

Scheduling and amdgpu waves: llvm.amdgcn.sched_barrier(0x0008) prevents MFMA/WMMA reordering across barrier - use to protect double-buffer sync. sched_group_barrier(mask,size,syncID) for custom pipelines. Also set amdgpu-waves-per-eu via __launch_bounds__ MIN_WARPS and via compile flag -mwavefrontsize64 vs 32. For gfx1100, compile with --offload-arch=gfx1100 -mllvm -amdgpu-enable-lds-bank-conflict-check.

Throughput validation path: CPU smoke → partial -ngl → full -ngl per AGENTS.md critical operational rules. Validate WMMA kernel with hipcc --offload-arch=gfx1100 (ROCm 5.4+/6.4+) or via Orochi hipRTC at runtime. Use AMD Matrix Instruction Calculator (github.com/RadeonOpenCompute/amd_matrix_instruction_calculator) to validate VGPR mapping before committing to 1000 tok/s goal.
